parakeet: You ever notice how asking does God exist feels like asking is the tooth fairy paying my rent this month? It's a question that feels deep because we've been told it is. That question assumes that the concept was ever meaningful enough to deserve verification, that it came from evidence, from sincere inquiry, from something real. But it didn't. It came from pattern-seeking brains in a thunderstorm. It came from fire-lit stories and tribal fears, from agency detection, your brain seeing a rustle in the bushes and assuming it's a predator. Not because it was, but because it could have been. That's where God was born, not in miracles, in maybes, not in revelation, in reaction. Humans didn't discover gods, we invented them. Because fear plus ignorance equals meaning if you say it loud enough. So now we're here centuries later, still treating that speculation like it deserves cross-examination, still pretending the courtroom is full when nobody ever showed up to testify. That question, does God exist, is not a starting point. It's a distraction. Long before Moses allegedly claimed stone tablets, before Jesus supposedly broke bread, before the Quran dropped bars in the desert, there were lightning strikes, predators in the dark, children dying for reasons no one could explain. And in those moments, what did we do? We reached for stories. We projected minds into the unknown. We didn't understand the storm, so we imagined a storm God. Didn't understand death, so we invented a gatekeeper on the other side. And don't get it twisted. This wasn't evil, it was adaptive. When you're trying to survive without science, reason becomes optional, and comfort becomes mandatory. Here's the twist, though. Those gods didn't evolve from truth. They evolved from terror. Gods didn't descend from heaven, they climbed up out of fear. Now ask yourself: if a belief starts as a survival tactic, does that make it true or just temporarily useful? Because let's be honest, most deities sound less like universal truth and more like emotional life rafts we kept patching up with dogma.
